title: stapler-squad: terminal experience
description: Where does terminal input lag come from? Keystroke-to-echo broken into send, server, network and render; backend call decomposition; head-of-line waits on every hop; queues, drops, runtime.

links.title: Slow-call traces in Tempo (Explore)
links.tooltip: Spans exist only for calls over the slow-call threshold

panels.title: Alerts: red here means the user is feeling it
Echo paint p95
panels.description: Keystroke to painted echo, browser-measured. Red above the 150 ms alert limit.

panels.title: Server input p95
panels.description: Keystroke frame read -> backend send returned. Red above 100 ms.

panels.title: Slow calls / min
panels.description: capture_pane, resize, write_stdin or send_keys calls slower than STAPLER_SQUAD_SLOW_CALL_MS (250 ms).

panels.title: Dropped frames / min
panels.description: Output frames dropped on a full hub or tymux queue. Any sustained value is a visible glitch.

panels.title: Event-loop lag p95
panels.description: Worst main-thread timer drift per 5 s window, browser-measured. A busy thread delays every keystroke.

panels.title: Scheduler latency p99
panels.description: Go goroutine run-queue wait. Above 100 ms the server itself is starved.

panels.title: Keystroke to echo: where does the lag sit?
Echo painted (browser) p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Keystroke sent -> echo painted two animation frames later. The number the user feels.

panels.title: Echo written (server) p50 / p95 / p99 by backend
panels.description: Keystroke received on the server -> next output frame written to the socket. Compare with the browser panel: the gap is network plus browser.

panels.title: Echo breakdown (mean, stacked)
panels.description: Averages add up, percentiles do not. send queue = browser send queue; server = echo_server; network+return = echo_arrive - server - send queue (clamped at 0); render = arrive -> painted.

panels.title: Server input path p95 by stage
panels.description: Inside one keystroke on the server: bookkeeping, waiting for the Attach stream lock, the stream Send, and the whole input_total.

panels.title: tymux echo_server decomposition (mean, stacked)
panels.description: Where the server's echo time goes on tymux, tymux sessions only. echo_daemon needs a daemon with capability output.sent_at (v1.17.0+) and is empty otherwise, and it contains stream_lock_wait and stream_send. echo_daemon and output_transit attribute the first stamped frame after a keystroke, an upper bound under bulk output, so the stack only approximates the echo_server line. Averages add; percentiles do not.

targets.legendFormat: pty write + app echo + daemon send queue (echo_daemon)

panels.title: Backend calls: capture_pane / resize / write_stdin / send_keys
Operation latency p50 / p99 by backend
panels.description: session.backend.* durations, the sum of everything below.

panels.title: tymux capture_pane decomposition (mean per capture)
panels.description: Mean per capture call. total = rpc + render + revive + squad-side. squad-side is the residual: time spent outside the RPC, render and revive (locks, queueing, retries). Render and revive are spread over every capture, so revive is ~0 unless a pane was dead.

panels.title: tmux capture_pane decomposition (mean)
panels.description: tmux has no single RPC: exec-gate wait, subprocess exec, and control-mode command round trip are measured separately.

panels.title: tymux RPC round trip p50 / p99 by method
panels.description: Pure gRPC wall time of one tymuxd control RPC (needs the tymux_rpc_duration_ms build).

panels.title: Slow calls by session
panels.description: Calls over the slow-call threshold per minute, by op and session. Only the 20 busiest sessions per 10 minutes keep a name; the rest are 'other'. Open the same time range in Tempo for the span (name = the op).

panels.title: Contended Instance lock waits (pm_lock_wait)
panels.description: Waits on Instance.pmMu. Only contended acquisitions are recorded, so the count is how often typing met a lock.

panels.title: Browser <-> squad mux: HOL wait p50 / p99
panels.description: Time a frame waits behind others on the shared browser WebSocket (terminal_mux_hol_wait).

panels.title: Hub subscriber queue wait p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Squad: a frame sits in a subscriber's outbound queue (100 slots) until the writer takes it. Rising means the browser side is draining slower than output arrives.

panels.title: squad <-> tymux: frame handling and fanout wait p95
panels.description: tymux_frame_handle: daemon frame received -> fanout broadcast done. tymux_fanout_wait: broadcast -> PTY adapter reads it (64 slots). tymux_pty_write: adapter write into the PTY socketpair.

panels.title: squad -> browser socket: write wait and write p95
panels.description: Per-stream socket write lock wait and the write itself, plus hub output_send.

panels.title: Browser: send queue, socket backlog, event loop
panels.description: input_queue = keystroke enqueued -> handed to the socket (ms). eventloop_lag = worst timer drift per 5 s (ms). Socket backlog is in the next panel.

panels.title: Browser WebSocket backlog (bufferedAmount)
panels.description: KiB the browser had queued but not sent when a keystroke went out. Growth means the uplink or the mux socket is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Queue depth p99
panels.description: Frames waiting: hub subscriber outbound queue (cap 100) and tymux fanout queue (cap 64). Near the cap means drops are next.

panels.title: Dropped frames by cause
panels.description: Frames lost to a full queue. Each drop forces a repaint of that subscriber.

panels.title: Resyncs by reason
panels.description: Full-screen resync requests and client-side skips. Spikes after tab focus are the avoidable kind.

panels.title: Subscriber lifecycle
panels.description: Hub subscribers attaching, detaching and being evicted for being slow.

panels.title: Scheduler latency
panels.description: Goroutine run-queue wait (p50 and p99 as exported).

panels.title: GC pause and mutex wait
panels.description: GC pause quantiles and the share of time goroutines spend waiting on mutexes.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: A steady climb is a leak; a spike is a stall.

panels.title: DB pool wait p99 by database
panels.description: Time queries wait for a pooled connection. Terminal paths that touch the DB inherit this.

panels.title: Host pressure (cgroup)
panels.description: cgroup memory pressure (Linux hosts). Empty on macOS: no node-exporter data exists on this host.
